title: Senior's toolkit: the language
summary: The expressions, functions, meta-arguments and lifecycle settings experienced Terraform authors reach for, and the console tricks that make them easy to get right.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: the language
steps.body: Seniors try an expression in `terraform console` before they put it in a pull request, and they reach for `for_each` by default.

toolkit.what: Evaluate expressions with the real variables, locals and state.
flags: one answer, for scripts and quick checks
see what type a value has (Terraform 1.x console)
toolkit.example: echo '{ for n, s in var.servers : s.role => n... }' | terraform console -var-file=prod.tfvars

toolkit.cmd: for_each = { for k, v in var.m : k => v if v.enabled }
flags: a list of names becomes keys
toolkit.example: for_each = { for name, t in var.teams : name => t if t.tier == "gold" }

toolkit.what: Rename, move into a module, or switch count to for_each without destroying.

flags: the iterator is named after the block

toolkit.what: How (and whether) Terraform replaces a resource.
flags: fail any plan that destroys it

toolkit.what: Fail fast on bad input and bad assumptions; warn about the world.
Defaults and optional data without errors.
flags: first expression that does not error
a map value with a default

steps.prompt: Match the need to the construct.
pairs: named instances that can be added and removed one by one
fail when prod has fewer than 2 replicas
warn when a certificate expires soon

code: echo 'merge({ a = 1, b = 2 }, { b = 3 })' | terraform console
steps.explain: `merge` combines maps; for a key in more than one, the last map wins. It is how modules layer default tags under the caller's tags: `merge(local.default_tags, var.tags)`.

steps.prompt: A reviewer sees `ignore_changes = all` on an `aws_instance`. What is the risk?
options: Terraform stops noticing any change to the instance, including your own changes in the code: it only ever creates it
It disables state locking for that resource
None; it is the recommended default
steps.explain: `all` turns the resource into "create once, then never manage". It is occasionally right (a resource handed to another tool after creation), but usually it hides drift and makes code changes silently do nothing. Name the attributes.
